summary: Frontend-only E2E test of the expanded multi-service PORTAL. Registered new unpaid user qav3878783@example.com. Verified: sidebar nav (all 7 testids), portal-dashboard with 6 dashboard-cards + card navigation, AI Video studio intake + persistence, Voice AI studio intake + persistence, LLM Citation gating (free scan on linear.app -> 91 opportunities, generate-pages -> 402 -> error toast + redirect to /fractional-cxo#cxo-packs, /portal/pages shows pages-locked + pages-unlock-cta), CXO Hours empty state (0 hrs + buy CTA), Affiliate (3 tiers + CTA), full AI SDR removal (homepage Portal tabs=6 no SDR, /fractional-cxo estimator has 6 services + CXO, no 'SDR' string anywhere, totals recompute correctly), mobile pricing header cxo-nav-cta ('Book a call', no overflow), and auth-guard regressions. FOUND + FIXED one CRITICAL crash: /portal/video and /portal/voice were completely dead (white 'Application error: a client-side exception has occurred') because VideoStudio/VoiceStudio used useEffect(load, []) where load returns a Promise -> React threw 'destroy is not a function'. After the fix both studios work end-to-end. One HIGH UX bug remains for the main agent (onboarding modal blocks the pricing page that the paywall redirects to).

ui_bugs.issue: FIXED BY TESTER: useEffect(load, []) returned a Promise -> React 19 threw 'destroy is not a function', crashing the whole /portal/video and /portal/voice routes (blank 'Application error' page, video-studio/voice-studio never rendered). Changed to useEffect(() => { load(); }, []). Verified both pages now render, submit and persist.

critical_code_review_comments: Never pass an async/promise-returning function directly to useEffect (useEffect(load, [])) - React treats the return value as the cleanup fn and throws 'destroy is not a function', which crashes the entire route. PortalLeadsBoard.jsx:27 uses the same pattern but is safe only because its load() has a block body returning undefined; wrap it too for safety.
Portal gating logic is correct: /api/portal/access + 402 on generate-pages are both honoured client-side (error toast + redirect) and server-side; scan/opportunities remain free as specified.

rca_of_the_issue: VideoStudio.jsx/VoiceStudio.jsx defined `const load = () => fetch(...).then(...)` (arrow expression body) and then `useEffect(load, [])`. React stores the returned Promise as the effect cleanup and calls it on unmount/StrictMode double-invoke, raising 'destroy is not a function', which propagated as an unhandled render error and replaced the whole page with Next's client-exception screen. Fix: wrap in `useEffect(() => { load(); }, [])`. Re-tested: both studios render, submit (success toast), list the request with the correct 'Video generation in progress' / 'Building your agent' badge, and persist across reload.
